svg.title: Proof. Resolvent inversion gives ∥(E′)−1 −E−1∥op ≤δ/[s(s −δ)]. Undo the output conjugation Uj. Its superoperator differs from the old one by Oj[(E′)−1 −E−1], of Frobenius norm at most the second quantity in Eq. (48). Choi reshuffling preserves Frobenius norm and operator norm is no larger. Both maps have output on the same fixed plane Qj after undoing Uj; therefore the corresponding Choi perturbation is supported on the same six-dimensional subspace, not on an uncontrolled former zero eigenspace. It is Hermitian, because the map sends a Hermitian basis to Hermitian matrices. The positive eigenvalue gap thus proves CP and full rank six on this support. Each changed state column has Frobenius error at most 2 maxb ∥Ub −I∥, so δ ≤6 maxb ∥Ub −I∥proves the sufficient condition. Trace preservation holds on the basis because all states have trace one and ∑︁ j Taj = 1. Set τ ′ = 1
